narration: You think you're bad at grocery shopping. You're not — stores spend billions designing the exact purchases you're about to throw away.
visual: Person silhouette pushing a shopping cart; food items (apple, bread, milk) inside the cart with red X marks appearing one by one; dollar bills drifting toward a trash can below

narration: The average family wastes $1,600 in food every single year. That's 40 percent of everything you bought, straight into the trash.
visual: Animated dollar counter ticking up to $1,600; side-by-side bar chart — green bar labeled EATEN 60% and red bar labeled WASTED 40%; subtly growing trash can icon

narration: It's not a willpower problem. Stores use three specific psychological tricks to guarantee you overbuy every single time. Here's number one.
visual: Dark background with 'STORES USE 3 TRICKS' headline; three numbered circles spring in one by one labeled: BULK PACKS, LOSS LEADERS, EXP. DATES; circle 1 highlighted in red

narration: Number one — bulk packs. They feel like a deal. Buying in bulk raises how much you purchase by 50 percent, but how much you eat by only 30.
visual: Small grocery bag vs oversized CLUB PACK bag side by side; two animated progress bars — BOUGHT +50% in red, EATEN +30% in green; gap between them labeled WASTE

narration: Number two — loss leaders. Stores price milk and eggs below cost just to get you through the door. The six unplanned items in your cart? All profit.
visual: SVG storefront with entrance; milk jug and egg carton icons at entry with red SALE tags; shopping cart fills with 3 extra impulse items appearing one at a time

narration: Number three — expiration dates aren't safety deadlines. Retailers pick the date. Eighty billion pounds of good food gets trashed because of a number stores chose. Track what you toss for just seven days.
visual: Cereal box with a prominent expiration date label and a trash can icon; large stat '80 BILLION LBS WASTED/YEAR'; CTA button: 'Track your waste — save $800 this year'
